questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.**

The accused said to the judge, "Let me meet my children before I die, sir."

options.text: The accused requests the judge to let him meet his children before he died.
The accused requested the judge to let him meet his children before he died.
The accused begs the judge to allow him to meet his children before he dies.
The accused begged the judge to let him meet his children before he dies.

questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: The accused requested the judge to let him meet his children before he died.**

The reporting verb can either be 'requested’ or 'begged’ in the indirect speech. This leaves us with option 2 and 4. Since the speech was made in the past, the reported speech in the indirect speech must also be in past. Therefore, the verb must be 'died’. This leaves us with option 2, which is the correct answer.

questions.question: the birds of the East and _________ of the West.
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: those**

In order to refer to a specific thing previously mentioned, known or understood, we use 'that’ and 'those’. 'Those’ is the plural form of 'that’. Here, we use 'those’ to refer to 'the birds’.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

**If there is a**

X-corresponding sensation

Y-kind, there has to be a

Z-change in brain activity of a certain
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: ZYX**

If there is a change in brain activity of a certain kind, there has to be a corresponding sensation. Z cannot be the last phrase as it ends in an open note. Y cannot be the last phrase as it ends with the article 'a’ in an open note. Therefore, X is the last phrase. Y must come after Z as ‘a certain kind’ logically fits. The sequence is ZYX.

The use of irony to mock or convey contempt
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: Sarcasm**

'Sanction’ is to officially validate or approve something.

‘Compliment’ is a polite expression of praise and admiration.

questions.question: One cannot help ___________ into the speculative mood
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: falling**

The blank must be filled with a gerund, i.e., a verb that functions as a noun. The gerund form of ‘fall’ is ‘falling’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

She was uneasy because she (never be) on a plane before.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __had never been__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The past perfect, also called the pluperfect, is a verb tense used to talk about actions that were completed before some point in the past**.__**
 
• **Examples:**
 __
 
• The train** had just left** when I arrived at the station.
 
• She **had just left **the room when the police arrived.
 
• I **had just put **the washing out when it started to rain.
 
 
 
• The past perfect tense is for talking about something that happened before something else. 
 
• Here **'not been on a plane before'** is the first action, so should be in past perfect tense.

​**Thus, the correct answer is: ***She was uneasy because she **had never been**__ on a plane before.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.**

The fire destroyed the whole neighbourhood.

options.text: The whole neighbourhood is destroyed by the fire.
The whole neighbourhood was destroyed by the fire.
The whole neighbourhood was being destroyed by the fire.
The whole neighbourhood is being destroyed by the fire.

questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: The whole neighbourhood was destroyed by the fire.**

Here, the subject is ‘the fire’ and the object is 'the neighbourhood’. The verb 'destroyed’ will be replaced by 'was destroyed’. In the passive voice, the object is acted upon by the subjected. So the sentence must be: The whole neighbourhood was destroyed by the fire.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

**As for ourselves, we**

X-combing our hair 

Y-a good wash and 

Z-were contented with
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: ZYX**

As for ourselves, we were contented with a good hair wash and combing our hair. A pronoun is generally followed by a verb in the active voice. Z begins with the verb 'were’ and therefore comes first. Y cannot be the last phrase as it ends with a conjunction. Thus, the only possible combination is ZYX.

questions.question:

No one knows how he escaped (dash) to pieces.
questions.solution:

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the words/sentence.**

The upward force that a fluid exerts on a body floating in it
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: Upthrust**

‘Upthrust’ is the upward force that a liquid or gas exerts on the object floating in it.

'Plunge’ is to dive and jump quickly and energetically.

'Submerge’ is to cause something to be under water.

'Capsize’ is to be overturned in the water.

Thus, the answer is 'upthrust’.
